grand_strategy.reading: Hamas is a movement that lost the war it started and is trying to win the settlement. On the Luttwak reading, 7 Oct 2023 was an attack that destroyed its attacker's base and still redrew the map: Gaza is ruins, the military command was decapitated repeatedly (Deif, Yahya Sinwar, then his brother), Hezbollah and Iran were crippled, yet the Palestinian question is back on the table, recognitions of Palestine multiplied in 2025 and a US president personally owns a plan for Gaza. The cost of that outcome falls on Hamas, because every route to the state it helped bring back runs through its exclusion and its disarmament. Its strategy in 2026 is therefore delay with concessions on form: it gives up the hostages (the last bargaining chip, spent between 13 Oct 2025 and early 2026), dissolves its administration, accepts a technocratic committee and says yes to the 15-point roadmap, but holds the weapons and the tunnels as insurance, and tests whether the Board of Peace can force Israel to leave the Yellow Line first. Israel reads the same facts the other way (no withdrawal until disarmament), so the ceasefire exists on paper and bleeds on the ground: Hamas has not disarmed, Israel holds about 60% of the Strip, no stabilisation force and no technocratic committee has entered, and Israeli strikes on commanders have escalated since Sep 2026 ahead of Israel's 27 Oct election. Underneath sits a leadership choice made in July 2026: Hayya, the negotiator close to Iran, over Meshal, the Qatar-leaning pragmatist. The patrons are weaker or squeezed (Iran at war, Qatar bombed and pressed, Turkey vetoed from the force, Egypt hostile to Brotherhood rule), and the rival Palestinian Authority has just postponed the elections that might have given Hamas a legitimate way back. One signal that is not a row: Hamas announced a pause in public executions on 21 Oct 2025, days after Trump threatened to 'go in and kill them', so the order it keeps is partly a function of Washington's attention.

stances.note: Mortal enemy on both sides: Hayya said on 15 Jan 2025 that Hamas would keep pursuing Israel's end and expel 'the occupation' from all of Jerusalem and the land; in Apr 2024 a state on the 1967 lines was offered only as a temporary stage; and Israel's declared aim since 7 Oct 2023 is Hamas's elimination (Netanyahu and Katz claimed the killing of al-Beik on 29 Sep 2026, Netanyahu rejects any Hamas or PA role in the 'day after' and says there is no withdrawal until Hamas disarms). The ceasefire of 10 Oct 2025 has not changed the structure: 1,481 Palestinians killed in its first year and Israel holding about 60% of the Strip. Symmetric with Israel's own reading, as the build expects. Bond: grievance.
